inspiration.display: ecology / niche partitioning + statistics + scheduling theory

why_interesting: The problem's 'Scheduling' dimension (how work is assigned to the available resources) is where the conventional approach carries a structural assumption: A single centralized scheduler must gather global state before it can decide, so its decisions are always slightly stale under fast-changing loads. AARL took a mechanism that already works in ecology / niche partitioning, statistics, scheduling theory - Treat non-uniform participants as exploitable structure instead of averaging them away. - and asked what happens if it is applied to GPU. If the mechanism transfers, the gain would come from removing that assumption rather than from tuning the existing design. Whether it transfers is exactly what is not established here.

first_experiment.objective: Establish whether the mechanism moves resource utilization for GPU at all, before tuning anything.
first_experiment.design: Baseline A: the conventional scheduling approach. Variant B: the Heterogeneity awareness mechanism applied only to the scheduling dimension. Keep every other parameter identical and use the same seed/warm-up.
first_experiment.decision_rule: Only claim support if B moves resource utilization outside the run-to-run spread of A; if the spread is larger than the effect, report INCONCLUSIVE rather than a direction.
first_experiment.what_would_make_it_stop: If A is already at the physical or structural limit of resource utilization, the comparison cannot discriminate and the design must change.
